lines: Every trade, every kindness, every cruelty. Someone <bold>writes it down</bold>.
The best clue I ever found was written in a margin by someone annoyed.
Someone once returned a book cleaner than they borrowed it. We still discuss it.
There is a story from the lectern, but it sounds smaller unless you were standing there.
Once a ledger solved an argument that three witnesses had made worse.
A child hid a beetroot in a book and called it a pressed flower. It was not.
I found an old map folded inside a cookbook. It explained several bad meals.
During a storm, everyone came to the library because paper made the rain sound smaller.
A villager once returned a book cleaner than when it left. I still suspect magic.
The oldest shelf here creaks at gossip and stays quiet for poetry.
I once chased loose pages across the square and lost one to a puddle with ambition.
A trader asked for a book about courage and bought one about knots by mistake.
There was a week when every missing book was under the same chair.
I saw a recipe save a festival after confidence nearly ruined the stew.
Someone used a history book to press leaves and accidentally learned something.
A bell rang during story hour and every child remembered where the doors were.
I once repaired a page that had survived rain, ash, and someone else's lunch.
A poem made the blacksmith cry once. They claimed it was smoke.
The quietest book here has started the loudest arguments.
